utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that the Prosecution wanted to raise a preliminary matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. This is in respect of the matter that the Trial Chamber reminded the Prosecution the other day had not been resolved with respect to MFI 745, and the Trial Chamber requested a response by the 27th of August. By way of quick backdrop, this document, MFI 745, was tendered through Witness Vlaski and, at the time, the Prosecution asked the Defence about its provenance. The Defence did not have such information at the time and advised the Chamber that the document should be MFI'd pending further information. On -- in May of this year, the Defence advised the Prosecution that the document was provided to Vlaski by the Serbian security service; that was the further information we were provided. Now, we note in respect of that information that the document bears no facial indicators of Serbian DB origin, such as a header or a stamp of the type that appear in other documents of allegedly similar provenance. We also note that had we been advised at the time of the Mr. Vlaski's assertion that he received it from the Serbian DB, we would have asked the witness about the circumstances of that alleged transfer as well as his relationship to the DB. While we consider that these factors clearly bear on any weight that can be attributed to the document, we do not, in the interests of comity, oppose the admission of the document on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Tieger. No other preliminaries. Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration, Ms. Radovanovic, you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. File will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: When we left off yesterday, we were discussing whether you had written a scientific journal article that had been accepted for publication after an international peer-review process. You had indicated that you had one from a journal of the Russian Academy of Science but could not recall the precise title or the year of the publication. Thank you for subsequently providing the details of this publication which my office received yesterday afternoon. If we could have 65 ter number 33044, we'll see the document that we received. If we could please go to e-court page 2. At the top, it says NGO Srebrenica historical project, the Netherlands. And then you have the publication title which is: International Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia: Activity, results, impact. And then it says: "Proceedings of the international scholarly symposium at the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow, April 22 to 23, 2009, in collaboration with the Centre for the Study of the Contemporary Balkan Crisis of the Institute for Slavic Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences. At the bottom it is indicated it was published in Belgrade and Moscow in 2010. Could we go to e-court page 4, please. If you look at the masthead for the people managing this publication, the editor-in-chief is an individual named Stephen Karganovic and the scholarly advisors are Dr. Nenad Kecmanovic, and Dr. Edward Herman. Are you familiar with these individuals personally?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Dr. Nenad Kecmanovic, I know him by reputation only. I've never met him. As for Dr. Edward Herman, I don't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And Stephen Karganovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do know him, but I only met him when -- actually, I met him before he invited me to the symposium once here in The Hague and then his invitation followed to his international gathering. It was much later. At some point much later than the time when I met him here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Just to clarify, when was the first time you met him?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met him for the first time when I arrived here concerning the Popovic case. At the time, he worked for or collaborated with attorney-at-law, John Ostojic, and that's when I was able to meet him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Did you --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- perhaps I went to Counsel Ostojic's office here to discuss matters and I met Stephen Karganovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So he was the one who invited you to present a paper at this conference?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me if I was willing to come and I received an official invitation from the Slavic studies centre of the Russian Academy of Sciences he simply gave me a phone call to inquire whether I was willing to participate and contribute to this or that topic. The official invitation was received from the Russian Academy of Science, its institute for Slavic studies.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go to e-court page 6, please. Now at the top of the page you can see your paper in the table of contents. The title of the paper you presented there was: Demographic Expert Reports of the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor as a Specific Model of Targeted Statistical Constructs and Manipulations. That was the title of your paper and the presentation at the conference; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood it yet the way it was interpreted. My article was entitled demographic expertise of the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor as a specific method or model of targeted statistical constructs and manipulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. You can see other papers presented that are listed on this page, including topics like the third one down from the top about: Violation of Vojislav Seselj's procedural rights at the ICTY. And at the bottom, you can see one titled: How The Hague tribunal ignores facts and evidence. Were you present at the conference to hear those papers presented?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So just to be perfectly clear: You physically went to the Russian Academy of Science in Moscow and attended the conference there in April of 2009?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I also presented my paper and was present while the other authors presented theirs.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So you were a conference participant?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, did you remember attending this event when I asked you about your publications yesterday and you mentioned the Russian Academy of Science but said you couldn't remember the exact title or year?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You didn't ask me if I attended the conference or not. You asked me whether I published something.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Right. Well, did you not consider it important to mention what you could remember about the facts or context in which you prepared and delivered this paper?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object to the question. That wasn't asked by counsel yesterday so asking for a witness to make comments on things that were not asked is really badgering the witness and is not in line with presenting the evidence that was presented yesterday. I would strenuously object to this line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied. The witness was asked whether she considered something yesterday which is a question of fact. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You can answer the question.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor asked me if I published anything in foreign journals, and I said yes, in the proceedings of the Russian Academy of Sciences although I was unable to recall the precise title or year. Then Judge Orie requested that I inquire, and then the discussion followed because the Internet did not occur to me since I'm not well versed in those terms when it comes to technology. I was simply not asked whether I participated in anything or presented anything, and that is how I managed to acquire this information. I'm grateful for those who reminded me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not attacked in any way, so there's no need to defend yourself. It's just a question, whether you have considered that. Apparently, because you thought it was not related to the question, you did not consider that. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I wasn't defending myself. I was merely responding to the question the way I understood it. Nobody asked me if I participated anywhere. I was asked whether I published anywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You have not answered my question to you, but I deduce that you didn't think this information to be directly related to the question that was put to you. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So this publication is a book that is a collection of papers presented at the conference; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So the paper that appears here that you wrote was not internationally peer-reviewed in the sense that did you not submit it to a scientific journal so that it would be reviewed anonymously by demographers or statisticians in order to determine whether to accept it in the journal. You were invited to present this paper by Mr. Karganovic?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was personally invited by the Russian Academy of Sciences. As for Mr. Karganovic he only inquired preliminarily whether I wanted to take part or not. He wasn't the one to decide whether I would be invited.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Ma'am --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- following his inquiry, I submitted my report, my paper. As for what you say that following the event I could have given my paper to a journal to have it reviewed by those you consider competent, well, if a paper is published anywhere and then if you offer it in the same form to someone else, it's a no-go because it had been published previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And please do not take this to be any kind of defence on my part but I just wanted to add something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would limit yourself to answer the question because are you dealing with a lot of matters which are not, at least we understand not to be part of the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Let's try it one more time. The paper that appears here that you wrote, that was published in this book, was not internationally peer-reviewed in the sense that you did not submit it through a peer-review process for it to be published here?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Object as to the form of question. Mixing and matching two different things. He starts off talking about international peer review. I would like to have a citation for international peer review as being a rule for expert evidence that's required. I'm familiar with peer review which is what all the literature on the topic talks about. The second part of his question switches from international peer review and starts talking about peer review. In that manner, that question is confusing and inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep matters short. The contribution to the conference as published was not peer reviewed before it was presented or published; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not correctly understood. You can see here who reviewed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was that prior to publication that others looked at it and gave their comment in order to either give the green light or -- to perhaps give the green light for publication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Reviews are always done prior to publication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Who reviewed this prior to publication?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, papers that are being reviewed are coded. In other words, no one is duty-bound to tell you who the reviewers are. However, once the proceedings are published, then usually the reviewers are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, what you're saying cannot possibly be correct. Given that this book is a collection of papers that were presented at a conference. It's not a journal of statistics, it's not a journal of demography, it's a conference and this is a collection of papers that were the proceedings; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But at an internal conference. When international conferences are being organised then, according to the rules, we need to know who the organisers are, who are the reviewers for the papers, what sections individual authors will take part in. No international conference can be set up ad hoc. There are procedures. Have a look at any kind of documentation concerning an international conference and its proceedings subsequently and can you figure it out. In order for me to explain it all, it would take time. But, in short, an international conference cannot be organised ad hoc, especially if it involves people from different countries. No one applies because they like to do so per se. People have to apply and then, in the organising committee of the conference, there are people who divide papers per section and by content. They say, This is a go; that is a no-go; this will go to that section; that will go to the others. I don't have the list of people who were --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you just said people had to apply. But you didn't have to apply. You were invited; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean I didn't have to apply? Mr. Karganovic said, There will be a conference in Moscow at this and that place. Do you want to participate? I said I do. Then I received a letter from the institute of Slavonic studies of the Academy of Sciences where they say that they intend to organise a conference on that topic and to take place on this and that date. They asked also if I was willing to contribute through a paper, and I said yes. Then you need to send the title and a summary. After a while, they ask you for your full paper. I followed the procedure. Following it all, I was invited to attend the conference to present my paper. I could have sent my paper without presenting it, but I consented to being there.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Are you aware that one of the scholarly advisors for this publication, Dr. Nenad Kecmanovic, appeared in this trial as a Defence witness?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I do know that Dr. Kecmanovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- was in some other --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the paper that you presented there and published in this collection of articles. It contained themes that were very similar to what you have presented in your expert report in this case; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see that it involves demographic expert reports by the OTP. I have to stick to the topic. I can't discuss any other demographic expert reports other than those of the OTP. It referred to those expert reports which had been published up to that moment in 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So I take it your answer is, yes, it did cover the same [Microphone not activated]?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then I must have misunderstood your question. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I asked you if it contained the same or similar themes as what you've presented in your expert report in this case.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no similar or same topics. There may have been similar criticisms levied as presented here as well. But it has to do with Srebrenica and the expert reports. I don't recall off the cuff which expert reports they are that I took into account though.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter number 33050. This is going to be the conclusion to this publication that contains the conference recommendations. For this, we're going to look at e-court page 3 and B/C/S page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Page 3 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: In the first paragraph, under conference recommendations, this is at the bottom of the page in B/C/S and the top of the page in English, it says: "Conference participants embraced the conclusion that ICTY should be shut down immediately and that all its activity must be subjected to serious review. In addition to crude violations of international law and ICTY's own rules of procedure, the principle of rebus sic stantibus is in itself sufficient to effect the Tribunal's immediate abolition." Now if we skip down two paragraphs it says as follows: "The responsibility of Judges and other Tribunal personnel for violations of international law and of the Tribunal's own rules of procedure should be raised and actively pursued. "The issue of Srebrenica and the so-called genocide of Muslim civilians and military personnel must be subjected to comprehensive and exhaustive analysis in light of new facts and of all disposable evidence. "Particular attention must be given to the case of General R. Krstic, where ICTY, acting without any justification, classified events in Srebrenica in July of 1995 as genocide." Those were some of the conference recommendations of the conference where you were a participant; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they have to do with me. These are obviously recommendations but I didn't participate in the drafting of these conclusions and I never signed this. I told you, every conference has certain persons who do certain things. Nobody offered those conclusions to me there and now whether they were drawn there, I don't know. I never signed any one of these conclusions. I signed my paper. Now, what somebody is going to conclude on that basis, well, no one ever asked me any such thing. I really have nothing to do with any of that. Just like I don't know what people here are going to conclude about me. That has nothing to do with me. I have nothing to do with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I just want to return to how you addressed this yesterday afternoon. At T38290, I asked you whether it was still true that: "Have you not published any articles in scientific journals that were the subject of international peer review before publication." Your answer was: "No, it's not correct. I just didn't write this again. In the meantime, I published in a journal of the Russian Academy of Science. I suppose you would treat that as international." Now, Dr. Radovanovic, no reasonable scientist would consider this a scientific journal. There was no peer-review process and this has nothing to do with your field of demography and statistics. This is a book whose sole purpose is to denounce this Tribunal, and I put to you when you answered my question yesterday you did so untruthfully. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, compound question. Misstates the evidence and misstates the question that was asked. If you're going to cite to the question, read the question. You're starting in the middle of your question, counsel. If you're going to read the question, the question says: "Is your answer in the Prlic case still correct?" She said what she said. She testified today about how the paper was submitted, therefore you are misstating the evidence and you're asking a compound question that requires 15 different answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's not the case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is granted. Ms. Radovanovic yesterday testified about an article she published and you're now taking here to the conclusions of a conference of which the witness now testified that she was not involved in drawing those conclusions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, when I asked you yesterday whether you had published articles in scientific journals that were the subject of international peer review before publication, did you consider this document a scientific journal?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do I consider the document to be a scientific journal? I don't understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: This book that we're talking about here, do you consider it a scientific journal?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, that's a lot, isn't it? I'm not competent to say whether something is a scientific journal or not. I cannot do that on my own. There is a procedure involved that says whether something is a scientific journal or not. I cannot be the judge of that. I cannot judge whether a journal is scientific but I absolutely assert that it was an international conference and that a certain number of scholars took part in it from different fields. If you have a review by international experts or some experts that you considered to be competent and if they wrote that this is not an international journal, I will accept that. I do not consider myself to be that competent for everything, so that I could assess whether each and every paper here is scientific or not. I believe that the conclusion has nothing whatsoever to do with me and it's certainly not science, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We could not understand the last part of the sentence. Could the witness please stay a bit away from the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last part of the last sentence, and could you stay slightly away from the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the conclusion that was presented here is not a scientific conclusion because I don't know whether it was drawn from some other scientific papers that are mentioned. I really do not know about procedural law. Many papers were not from my field, and I cannot say whether they are scientific or scholarly papers or not. I can see who the authors I can see what these do otherwise but I really do not consider myself to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I invited you to repeat the last part of the last sentence, but you started a new answer. Mr. File, you should move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If we can turn to your report in this case. On page 3 in both versions, you have a heading entitled, "Reports analysed" and there you list 21 documents that you analysed as part of this project.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's D1211, MFI, I think for Your Honour's assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, could we have it on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it's 1211.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's correct. If we could have page 3 of both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You can see there's a heading entitled, "Reports analysed." And there you list 21 documents that you analysed as part of this project. Would you agree that you reviewed these documents carefully?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would agree that I reviewed these documents carefully.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to ask you about some of the tables that you included in your report. If we could please go to English page 47, B/C/S page 46, and this is not for broadcast. As this comes up you're going to see that this is Table 5 where you've listed 34 individuals together with their date and place of disappearance and their grave-site. The source for the information in this table is listed as the 2009 OTP list. After this table in your report, you express scepticism about the fact that they are listed as having been located in grave-sites in Serbia or "unknown," and you say in that paragraph just beneath the table: "All the above persons are on the Prosecution's list as Srebrenica victims because they are registered as missing in July and August in the places that the expert links with Srebrenica. If these people [sic] really went missing in July and August and were last seen alive in the registered places of disappearance, does it mean that they were taken to Serbia and killed there, and who killed and buried them there? Where and what are these unknown graves where Srebrenica victims were buried?" Now in the introduction to your report that we were just looking at, one of the documents you listed as having reviewed was the July 2013 research note called "Integration of the 2013 ICMP update with the 2009 OTP list of Srebrenica victims"; correct? And, for the record, we're talking about P2794. We're talking --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please tell me what number it is, what you mentioned just now in the literature there? I'm unable to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: It's number 20 at the bottom of page 4. We're talking about page 4 of your report --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it. I do see it. Dr. Ewa Tabeau: "The integration of the 2013 ICMP update with the 2009 OTP list of Srebrenica victims." Yes, I reviewed it very carefully. Of course, I could not --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- go to the list itself and check it, but that is in the list submitted by Dr. Brunborg. And, down there, it says very properly what the source is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can we go to P2794, page 7, please. You see at the bottom of the page it says: "Attachment: Excel file: Integration of 2013 ICMP update on Srebrenica and Zepa." And then it describes what is included there. Is it your testimony that you didn't look at that?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. This integrated one has to be sent as a new one and you cannot tell me here you are, a list from 2009 and then I'm going to tell you that something I put together in 2013, some things I threw out and other things I did not and you have to tell me what it is. If you made an integrated list in 2013, then it has to be corrected and it has to be corrected in the list of Srebrenica victims. I can trust Dr. Tabeau, but I do not see this correction in the list of Srebrenica victims and I don't know whether some day in the future again, it's going to be the list from 2009 and whether there is a list from 2013. That is to say, if you are updating something, you do not updating it by mentioning what you did in one part.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But this list that you present, that is being updated. What is being thrown out of there, what is being kept and --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: My question was very simple. I was just asking you if you reviewed this excel file when you were preparing your report.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reviewed everything I had. I reviewed the list of cases but I repeat once again --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Witness, the question was not whether you reviewed everything you had but whether you reviewed this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I read and reviewed the expert report, I reviewed this as well. It's cases that were found at such and such places but these cases were not put into the general list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that you reviewed this document as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So if we can go back to the list we were looking at, Table 5, which is English page 47 ... oh, in D1211, MFI. English page 47; B/C/S page 46. Again, not for broadcast. So where it says at the bottom of this table that the source is the 2009 OTP list and there's no reference to the 2013 update, it's correct to understand that the information you excerpted from the 2009 list here has not been checked or does not incorporate 2013 updates; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am not denying that they updated this in 2013, that they found some cases that they want to delete from the list that they published in 2009. However, in this list of 2009, they did not delete that. Now do they have a new list in which they deleted that? That I don't know. But it hasn't been attached. So I am referring to the original list of victims. For me to delete cases that Dr. Tabeau refers to, no way. There must be a list from 2013 that was updated. Therefore, it cannot contain 7.600. Never mind. But when you say updated list of cases then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, I do understand that any corrections that are not included in a new consolidated list that you consider that you don't have to mention those corrections and you are not bound to include it in your considerations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I must say, I'm confused. I'm looking at the annex to 2794 and I fail to see any of the names from this list so I'm confused by counsel's question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is perhaps the next question whether there was any reason to -- but we're still one step before that. There's no consolidated list, you are telling us, and, therefore, you relied on the 2009 and have not included the 2013 update in your comments. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, well understood. You understood that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I also just want to confirm that you did not look at the report of former OTP investigator Dusan Janc entitled: Update to the summary of forensic evidence, exhumation of the graves and surface remains, recoveries related to Srebrenica, June 2013, which is in evidence in this case as P1987. You did not review that report; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That report has to be reviewed by your experts. I could, but I don't have to do it. I can -- if your experts mention something -- no well, any way. I did not review it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... yes, that's an answer to the question and whether you were bound to do it [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... I did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because the other question is a different one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we please have 65 ter 33042 not for broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: These are the 34 individual that appear in Table 5 of your report. We've expanded your table, we've kept the names in the same order that you used, but we included additional information that can be found in the 2013 update. All of the information on this table is already in evidence in this case either in P1901, the 2009 list, where it indicates on the screen ICRC, or P2795, which is the 2013 integration where it indicates on the screen ICMP in the top columns, on the top row I mean. Just as a side note, I would also note in this chart we kept your original spellings of the names from Table 5 although you made two typographical errors when recording the names, these are noted in the first two footnotes on page 2, but it was possible with a visual inspection to determine which records you were talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, we have now heard 12 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have that, what you have been speaking just now. I don't have that on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. You've given comment now for some ten lines. If you would put a question to the witness that would be appreciated.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we could look at the top of the list on page one under Serbian sites --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Here you can see the first 16 individuals listed in your chart; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have Serb locations anywhere in the heading. I don't know if we're looking at the same table.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that the table we're looking at. I mean, it doesn't say Serbian sites anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That was not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're going to try to avoid using the names in these records. If you would, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise. I do apologise. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could you -- you have your report in front of you in hard copy form. If you --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Just tell me which page.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Page 46.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: You'll see that the first 16 people listed in that table in your report are also the first 16 people listed in this table; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can take your word for it. I can do all the counting now, all 16 and check, but I believe it when you say that that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And if you look on the screen in front of you, towards the middle it says: Site name. And for those 16 individuals you see the same site names in Serbia that are in your table, Table 5; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I would like to you look at the name of the person listed at record 8 without saying it, as well as his ICMP case ID and the site name, and I'd like you to find that record on the table in your report. In the -- on the paper report in front of you, if you can find the corresponding name.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found number 8, if that's what you mean. Yes, found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, I want you to keep track of this information for record 8 because I'm going to show you as an example how to trace the basis for an assertion that someone like this is a Srebrenica victim and then I will ask you a question about it; is that understood?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm aware we're getting close to the time for the break, Your Honour. I'm wondering if we could go into private session briefly to confirm that we're talking about the same person and then it might be a good time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. We'll take a break first. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I put on the record that D1211, which was MFI'd, should have been MFI'd under seal and has this status from now on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Radovanovic, we'll now continue, but may I urge you to respond to the questions rather than to what you think may be on the mind of Mr. File, right or wrong, but we're interested in your answers to his questions. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we please have P1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As this comes up, this is the 2013 report of former ICTY OTP investigator, Dusan Janc, and if we could go to page 38 of the English and page 42 of the B/C/S, please. For context, this is Annex A of the report which provides a summary of each Srebrenica grave. In the middle of the page under "Serbian related," you see that Mr. Janc writes: "There are several individuals on Srebrenica missing list whose remains have been found in Serbia. According to the ICMP ... and documentation provided by the authorities of the Republic of Serbia, the mortal remains of these individuals were found in different locations along the Drina or Sava riverbank." Just below, we see a chart of three Serbia-related locations; Sremska Mitrovica, Sabac and Beograd. Those are the same three names of graves in Serbia, listed in Table 5 of your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're probably the same, Sremska Mitrovica, Sabac and Belgrade, plus the unknown locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay, I'm focussing only on the Serbian ones now, not the unknown ones. Under the column for code in the Sremska Mitrovica row, you can see the ICMP case ID for the person I asked you to keep in mind earlier, record 8 on your list; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I did not memorize the code, but I absolutely believe that is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 33043, please. Also this one is not for broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, in the previous document, we saw Mr. Janc referring to document provided by the Serbian authorities. On page one of this document it says time and place of finding a corpse. If you look in the upper left-hand corner, do you see the same cases ID at the top for the person who is record 8 on your list?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not disputing that. I'm only asking how do they know it's related to Srebrenica. All I see here is that the institute for identification, according to their --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Identification methods which is DNA cannot know the time and location. But you claim that the doctor to whom you are referring claims this is Srebrenica related.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that wasn't the question. The question was a different one -- yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Orie, may I ask you something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not very usual, and I don't know whether I want to respond to whatever you want to say. But I urged you to answer the questions as put by Mr. File. The question was not on what basis someone would have related this corpse to Srebrenica. That may be an issue for this Chamber, and then we'll deal with that. It's not, at this moment, within the purview of your cross-examination. If there's anything apart from that you'd like to ask me, you have an opportunity to do so; but please keep in mind what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe it's not clear to me, but allow me to ask the question and then you will tell me if it is all right or not. I do not dispute whether a certain person is on the list. That's clear. I have one other question: On which basis is it maintained that this person is related to Srebrenica? The Prosecutor can show me simply that there is an explanation here for the relation with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Prosecution doesn't have to show that to you. They just put the question to you. And to the extent that question needs further attention, the Chamber will pay attention to it. Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As can you see at the top of this document, it says, "NN or unidentified male body was found on 19 July 1995 in the Sava river near the village of Bosut." Under the description of the body, it reads: "The body is in an advanced stage of decay, both of the outer tissue and the internal organs and the parts of the brains are missing." Further down, under autopsy, it reads: "It is noted that the death was violent. According to the pathologist's estimate the body stayed in the water for about eight days." Now if the body was found on 19 July and had been in the water for about eight days, that would take you back to 11 July 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File, don't ask for the obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: If we could go do page 2 of the English and page 8 of the B/C/S, please. I'd like to turn your attention to the second paragraph, which reads: "At the back of the head was found a perforated skin and skull defect continuing as a canal caused by a metal projectile fired from the small arm [sic], which is most probably a direct cause of death of an unidentified person." Do you see that written there?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And if we can turn to page 11 of the B/C/S and page 3 of English, please, here we see a criminal report filed on 25 September 1995 in Sremska Mitrovica. Turning to the next page in the English under description of the offence, please, it reads: "An unidentified perpetrator fired one bullet from an unknown fire-arms at the NN victim, inflicted gun-shot wound to his head and in that way took his life and then threw him into the Sava river. "On 19 July 1995 at the institute of forensic medicine in Novi Sad, an autopsy was carried out by pathologist, Dr. Simic, and at that time it was established that the death was violent and it was caused by gun-shot wound at the back of NN victim's head." Do you see that written there as well?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we please look at pages 3 to 4 of the B/C/S original side by side because we don't have a translation for these pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the page number.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: 3 and 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As you can see, these are photographs of the body as it was found on the riverbank. If we could please just zoom in on the bottom photograph on B/C/S page 4. We've not yet gotten this page translated, so could you please read aloud the text written below that photograph.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I can. It says: "Damage to the bone, bad." If I can make it out because it's a very difficult handwriting. "Damage to the bones of the corpse." "Of the corpse."

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Finally, could we please turn to page 5 -- page 5 in the original. This one is also not translated. Here we see the ICMP DNA report for this individual dated 25 May 2006 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Can you see the case ID in the upper left-hand corner that links this to the prior criminal investigation reports?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see this is a DNA report confirming that it was, indeed, that person we discussed earlier, and nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So my question to you is: Having seen this information, would you reconsider the scepticism expressed in your report as to whether remains found in Serbia can be associated with Srebrenica other than their date of disappearance?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would not have any proof that would indicate that, apart from the date of disappearance, and we know that dates of disappearance are very questionable and they contain many errors. Apart from the date of disappearance, there is no other fact or factual evidence that it is a person who was killed as a result of the events in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So am I right in understanding that you do not credit the ICRC report of a missing person as an indication of the circumstances of this person's death?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I object, that changes now the question. We've not seen the ICRC report. So if you're going to pose a new question, phrase it as a new question, not as a continuation of the previous question but as something different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're invited to rephrase your question, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: At the very beginning of discussing this subject, we saw a list of individuals who came from the OTP list of missing based on reporting by individual's loved ones, including this person, and so what I'm asking you is does that fact not factor into your conclusion as to available evidence of the circumstances of this person's disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object. We have looked at multiple lists. Can he specify the list. The one I remember was created by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We can talk about either P1901 which is the OTP list that presents the information as to where the missing persons report came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said either, about, and you mentioned one. I expect two sources.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Pardon me. The other source would the 2013 integration report which contains the same information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And which one identifies the source of that information as being loved ones?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say there may not have had a certain relationship as being a loved one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm saying the question as phrased --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Assumes facts not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Someone reports the person as missing --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you think it very relevant to criticise that they are concluded to be loved ones but they may not be.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it's confusing the issue when we're talking about this information that's not on the list. We have the particular list and we are basing data that's on the list, that's one thing. If we're adding things that are not in evidence, we're not getting --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think Mr. File has corrected his wording, loved ones, but the person who reported a person as having disappeared or went missing. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do, Mr. File, a few minutes ago you referred to an ICRC report which you asked the witness whether she doesn't consider that as a source. Are you moving away from the ICRC list now? Or are you -- are you -- now that you're talking about other lists --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The OTP list is a combination of the ICRC list and PHR list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps you put the question to the witness again now, and keeping in mind all the comments that were made on your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis that this individual was reported missing and is on the OTP list, does that factor into your conclusion that there is no other evidence linking this case to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the report of the ICRC and the report you mentioned here, the only evidence is the date. I do not see any other evidence because DNA does not prove when and where somebody died. DNA proves identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I think this will be a lot more simple if we return to 65 ter 33042. Before I do that, I would tender 65 ter 33043, which is the documentation we just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it should be MFI'd as we don't have a translation of the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no complete translation --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Agreed. Agreed. MFI'd, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, what number would be attached?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number 33043 receives exhibit number P7513, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So if we could return to 33042; also not to be broadcast, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Now, if you look again at record 8, you see there's another piece of information that comes from the ICRC. In addition to the date of disappearance, it's also the place of disappearance. And it says: "Potocari-Srebrenica." Would you consider that as a factor in your evaluation?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That information may be a factor in the estimate, but you know that your experts claim that many places are missing, that there are errors in the names and surnames, but I think it is acceptable. I don't know if corrections were made to the ICRC list, but I think that piece of information could be taken into account, but we could also take into account who is providing the information. That's the place where the person was last seen alive. It's not the place of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'd like to turn your attention to the bottom part of this list which starts at record 17. If you could look at those names. On this page, you can see -- the numbers are 17 through 21. And if you compare that with your Table 5 in your report, on page 46 of your report, you will see that those five names -- the first five names in your table which have a site name as unknown; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And can we go to the second page of this.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just have one thing to say. It's not my table. It's the table I took from Dr. Brunborg. I did not make a single table alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And for clarification, when I say "your table," I mean a table in your report. If you look at this list, which is the remainder from records 22 to 34, this is also the remainder of Table 5 in your report with site names designated as unknown in your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the table you're talking about, these are not sites. These are graves. Table number 5 that I took from Dr. Brunborg says graves, not sites. And then it enumerates graves in Mitrovica, Belgrade, and unknown graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Are you aware that where it says "site name" that that corresponds to grave-sites?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Grave-sites and graves are completely different concepts, but I'm not saying that it's not possible to use them interchangeably. In the material that I refer to as my source, it says graves, not grave-sites. In the materials that you are showing me now, it says place of disappearance. Your expert defines the place of disappearance as the place where somebody was last seen alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, that is not necessarily --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: We're not talking about place of disappearance.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are confusing me. Location, site, place of disappearance. I'm just trying to be detailed in my answers, to translate what I'm reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Is it your contention that the ICMP list of recovered DNA-identified individuals contains both a site name and a grave-site for each record?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand what you're asking me. Are you asking me in relation to the table which is on the screen now? Is that the question? Or are you asking me a general question?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep it simple. In your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. File, if I may, it looks like there's a confusion between place of disappearance which is right at the end, the last column and site name, ICMP, which is somewhere in the middle. Can you explain to the witness which of these two you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: For clarification, if you look at the top row, which is grey, in the middle you see a column that says, "site name, ICMP," and below it, you have words like Srebrenica, Kamenica, Bratunac, et cetera. And at the right-hand side of the screen --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: -- it says, "place of disappearance, ICRC". And below that, it says Potocari, Srebrenica, et cetera. And what I'm putting to you is that the ICMP site name column in the middle of the page corresponds to the column for grave-site in Table 5 of your report.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. In my report, in the tables provided by Dr. Brunborg, we find grave-site. These people, according to the ICMP, disappeared from the locations of Srebrenica, Kamenica, Liplja and so on and so forth. I do not dispute the fact that they may have disappeared at those locations. I'm simply saying that Dr. Brunborg lists grave-sites linking those to date and place of disappearance, as well as the site name provided by the ICMP, but he never explained that. If he concluded that the date plus place of disappearance plus ICMP information equals evidence that people were found in graves that are not at all in Srebrenica or Bosnia, then I would be able to understand, but he doesn't say that. In his list, he specifies the lists of Srebrenica victims and the grave-sites where the victims were found.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you for a second. Do I understand that the column with the heading, "site name, ICMP," refers not to the site of the grave what those persons were found? Is that your understanding of this table?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not my understanding. That is the case. The grave-sites may be at those locations, but they have completely different names or designations. There is no Srebrenica grave-site. But the ICMP did some things and they grouped some locations into municipalities or towns that they may belong to. Not all the grave-sites are in the territory of Srebrenica municipality. What we see here -- I apologise. What we see are not the designations of grave-sites but of locations. I do not dispute that perhaps there are some grave-sites in those locations though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: So, Dr. Radovanovic, I feel like we're talking about a distinction without a difference here. What I'm going to put to you is that now that ICMP has identified site names for all of these individuals with the exception of record 28 that you have listed with unknown grave-sites in Table 5, that that has resolved this question of whether their location of recovery is unknown. Is that how you understand it?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. I would have to read the report in more detail and analyse it in order to agree or disagree. If it is the case as you put it, then your expert must have provided a footnote and say, This is what happened according to this or that report or finding. But not inserting a footnote, the expert is confusing, not only me but the reader in general. If the expert borrowed it from another report then they have to reference it precisely. Off the top of my head I really can't decide. I would need to read the report as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to decide anything, Witness. The simple question was whether, on the basis of new information, right or wrong, with a footnote or without a footnote, that the unknown grave-sites have now been put as known grave-sites, although you may challenge that it's not with sufficient precision, et cetera, but the unknown is now replaced by known. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't have complete data.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. No, you don't have to prove anything. You just see unknown and in the other table it says what now the known site is. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please move on, Mr. File.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm struggling with your last answer and I would like to clarify. You say: I had no access to the new databases in these matters ..." utterances.text: If is an extraction were you able, Mr. File to offer a cup of tea or cup of coffee to Mr. Ivetic, and point where you extracted from those lists. I take it that the person [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, but if it's a demonstrative exhibit, does it need to be introduced into evidence [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Well, Mr. Ivetic, you are telling us that it takes such an effort to find in the other ones --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now it is offered to you that it's demonstrated. And now you're inviting the Chamber to find out for themselves what you apparently consider too much work.

utterances.text: Final question before we move on. Could we have 65 ter number 33041; also not for broadcast. Witness, if you would look at Table 2 of your own report on pages 36 and 37 --

utterances.text: -- and can you verify that you see on this list in the second column under names -- pardon me, in the third column under "names, ICRC," the same names that appear in your table? Up to line 17.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, now I need time to check all of this, but I'll take your word for it. I will believe that all of these are the same names.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. Can we go to page 2, please. And, again, the third column contains the remainder of the same names from your table; right?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's say that that's the way it is. Again, I'm taking your word for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: And what you see in the title column "case ID," towards the middle right part of the page, in some of these entries you see that there is a case ID; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you define what you mean by that? "Case ID"?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Well, the case ID that the ICMP would create for each located set of remains. You see that some of these records have those.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean, for example, in the case (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You shouldn't mention any name.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Please just use the number, please.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, please, I am so sorry. I do apologise. I'm getting old. If you mean where IT says, "case ID," yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And we've not had any questions as to this document that is presented as a demonstrative exhibit that go towards those ideas such that we can use it demonstrate something. A demonstrative exhibit is not something that is presented for the truth of matter asserted. This is being presented for the truth of the matter asserted without going though testimony or evidence to have it linked to be demonstrative in nature. So it is not a demonstrative exhibit in the manner that is being used by Prosecution counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, admission into evidence would assist the Chamber. At the same time, as with the previous table, it could be discussed over a cup of coffee or tea whether this is really an extract of what you claim it is an extract of, Mr. File. And you said it's the same as the previous one in respect exactly of what information? Site name or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: The cases ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The case ID, yes. If it's about linking the names to the case IDs, then I take it that a comparison of the more recent lists would assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to have it put on the record that having coffee or tea with the Prosecutor cannot change my position that this is not a demonstrative exhibit in the manner that is presented, and is being presented as argument for the truth of the matter asserted rather than demonstrating and being used with a witness in court to explain and understand the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This table assists the Chamber in finding easily and quickly those entries in the tables of the witness which seems not to fully correspond with the latest information on the other lists and for that purpose will be admitted into evidence. Madam Registrar, the number would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 33041 receives exhibit number P7517, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7517 is admitted into evidence, under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Okay. We no longer need this document. We're going to switch topics.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you about one of the major subjects of your report and testimony which relates to how Dr. Tabeau matched individual records from different data sources and which applies to Dr. Tabeau's analysis of both displaced persons as well as Srebrenica. In the context of the Srebrenica report, you discuss spelling errors and missing information occurring in more than 37 per cent, more than 37 per cent of the time in the ICRC and PHR lists; that's in your report D1211, at English page 38, B/C/S page 37. At that part of your report, you claim Dr. Tabeau is being "knowingly misleading," because "official statistical research tolerates deviation, possible errors, of up to 5 per cent." On Monday, at transcript page 38168, you said this error rate was 2 to 5 per cent. Then you said 2 to 4 per cent when you discussed the issue again at transcript page 38175 to 38177. But isn't it true that the 5-per cent guide-line is for the margin of error of statistical estimates, not the frequency of errors in raw data? Is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you said that I say 37 per cent. I'm not saying anything. I am just doing the calculations and quoting what your experts said. As for statistical error from 2 to 4, or 2 to 5 per cent, in my practice, in my country, it is 2 to 4. However, your expert, Dr. Tabeau, in her Mladic report, provides a methodology and when she speaks of certain matches, she says, This corresponds to what is considered statistical error from 2 to 5 per cent. So then I said, okay, let it be 2 to 5 per cent and that should not be in dispute. I agree with Dr. Tabeau that it can also be from 2 to 5 per cent --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- in statistics where I work, it is 2 to 4 per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: My question was related to a more specific distinction. I'm distinguishing between the margin of error for statistical estimates and the frequency of errors in raw data. The percentage that we're talking about here is a margin of error for statistical estimates, not the frequency of error in raw data; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I disagree with you. Read the paragraph carefully and you will see - at least this one that you've indicated - it is not an estimate. These are errors in data sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's exactly what Mr. File puts to you and that the margin of errors applies to the statistical estimates and not to errors in the raw material.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what I've said just now, I that that is not correct. This error is applied to raw data because that is how you assess whether your material is good or not. And if you establish that after all reviews, you still have a number that is larger than what is considered to be a normal statistical error, then that pertains to the raw data that you worked with. Not only in terms of estimates. Estimates are a specific thing, and you can have a margin of error -- well, I don't have to explain all of this now. This is something completely different. You cannot assess a single data source if you do not know what the error is. If you establish that the share is larger than permitted, then you have to make an effort, if at all possible, to reduce this to a permissible share. Here the Prosecution experts said what the margin of error that they established was. In 2009, in their report -- or, rather, in his report, Dr. Brunborg says, Now it is 28.9 per cent. So after all corrections, after everything they did. This is a margin of error of one-third.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: Could we look at 65 ter number 32997, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: As this comes up, you will see that it is a 2006 paper by William Winkler, a senior researcher in the Statistical Research Division of the United States Census Bureau. For the record, Dr. Tabeau cites this in her 2009 Srebrenica report, P1900, at page 70. If we could please go to e-court page 10. B/C/S is only a partial translation. I believe we need to go to page 2 of the B/C/S. Actually I don't see the translation for this one so this may have to -- we'll refer just to the English for now. In this article, doctor --

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have the translation in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to read you to the part, the relevant part.

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No offence, but I would prefer to see the translation, if possible, but if it's a problem, then I will just listen to the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you the paragraph under a heading entitled: String comparitors, which is 3.3. He writes: "In many matching situations, it is not possibly to compare two strings exactly (character by character) because of typographical error. Dealing with typographical error via approximate string comparison has been a major research project in computer science ... in record linkage, one needs to have a function that represents approximate agreement, with agreement being represented by 1 and degrees of partial agreement being represented by numbers between zero and 1. One also needs to adjust the likelihood ratios according to the partial agreement values. Having such methods is crucial to matching. For instance, in a major census application for measuring undercount, more than 25 per cent of matches would not have been found via exact character-by-character matching." And it goes on to say: "In the St. Louis region, for instance, 25 percent of first names and 15 per cent of last names did not agree character by character among pairs that are matches." So my question to you is: It is not unique or rare for statisticians to encounter an error rate in the underlying raw data that is well in excess of 5 per cent; correct?

utterances.speaker: SVETLANA RADOVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They have to deal with where the error is 5 per cent but the question is how they publish all of that. They do all of that at aggregate level. They never do that at individual level. And you see here? Statistics, as he says, I match such and such and what is right so on and so forth and I cannot match such and such a number as Dr. Tabeau says she cannot. The census of the US or any European country, and this method of matching, your expert, Dr. Tabeau, also explains that in the methodology provided for the report in the Mladic case, and she says hardly any country, if any, she doesn't say which one does it, rarely, carries out matching at individual levels as far as population censuses are concerned. Please, of course, I'm paraphrasing. I cannot say exactly. But I can bring it in later. Because data protection is very important there. So it's done according to --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. File --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do allow me to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: Apart from that, Mr. Ivetic, the proper way is to first answer the question and then if need be to explain especially if any further explanation is required. But it's not [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: Would you please not interrupt --

utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Overlapping speakers] ... I started answering and you didn't let me finish ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. As a matter of fact, I made my observations. That's it. It's not an incident. It's a repeated event during your testimony. Your observation is on the record, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then did you not let the witness answer the question, Your Honour, because your comments [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.text: Dr. Radovanovic, it's true and I think you can answer this with just a yes or no, it's true, isn't it, that you have not cited any scientific source like a journal article or a textbook anywhere in your report showing that standard statistical practice would not accept data with an error rate of more than 5 per cent. utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. Especially since Dr. Tabeau wrote that in her report when she was explaining the methodology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.text: I'd like to turn to page 25 of your report, D1211, MFI, under seal.

utterances.text: 25 in both versions.

utterances.text: Now if you see at the bottom of the page, again in both versions you say: "The personal identification number is a good matching key, provided that it is correctly written in both or several sources used."
